items.title: Three prices
items.prose: Three prices on a screen: £2.09, £2.1 and £2.089.
items.question: Which is the highest?

options.why: You picked the one with the most digits. Compare the tenths first: 1 beats 0.
You compared the last digits, 9 against 1. The tenths come first: 2.1 has 1 tenth, 2.09 has none.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Write each price to three places, then compare from the left.

explain.text: To three places the prices are 2.090, 2.100 and 2.089. All have 2 ones, and the tenths digits are 0, 1 and 0. So £2.1 is the highest.

byKey.digits: You wrote the 3 and the 4 side by side. Rewrite the fraction over 100 first.

items.title: A rise from below zero
items.prose: It is −6 °C at dawn. By noon the temperature has risen by 4 degrees.
items.question: What is the temperature at noon?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. A rise moves right from −6.

byKey.wrong-way: You moved left. A rise in temperature moves right.
byKey.lost-sign: You found the gap of 2 but put it above zero. Four steps right from −6 stop at −2.

explain.text: From $-6$, four steps right reach $-2$. So $-6 + 4 = -2$: still below zero.

items.title: Half a loss, reversed
items.prose: Use the sign rules with a decimal.
items.question: What is $(-8) \times (-0.5)$?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find the size, then the sign.

byKey.kept-minus: You kept a minus. Two negatives multiplied give a positive.
byKey.added: You added −8 and −0.5. The question multiplies them.
byKey.divided: You divided 8 by 0.5. Multiplying by 0.5 takes half, so the size is 4.

explain.text: Multiplying by 0.5 takes half, so the size is 4. Both numbers are negative, so the product is positive: $(-8) \times (-0.5) = 4$.

items.title: Sharing a fee
items.prose: A £20 fee is shared equally across 7 trades. Each share is charged to the penny.
items.question: How much is charged to each trade?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Divide 20 by 7, then round to two decimal places.

byKey.chopped: You cut after two places. The third digit is 7, so round up to £2.86.
byKey.unrounded: Charges stop at whole pennies. Round to two decimal places.
byKey.flipped: You divided 7 by 20. The fee of £20 is what gets shared.

explain.text: $20 \div 7 = 2.857142\ldots$, a recurring decimal. The third digit is 7, so it rounds up to £2.86.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Subtracting a negative moves right.

byKey.dropped: You took away 7.5. Taking away −7.5 is adding 7.5.
byKey.gap: You found the gap between 2.5 and 7.5. The two minus signs turn this into adding.
byKey.both-negative: You made the answer negative. Subtracting a negative moves right, so it gets bigger.

explain.text: Taking away $-7.5$ undoes a move of 7.5 to the left, so it moves 7.5 right: $2.5 + 7.5 = 10$.

items.title: Rounding to the penny
items.prose: An average price works out at £12.996.
items.question: What is it to the nearest penny?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find the two pennies either side, then pick the closer.

byKey.chopped: You dropped the 6. It is 5 or more, so the pennies go up.
byKey.carried-wrong: You wrote 100 hundredths as .100. A hundred hundredths make a whole pound, so it is £13.00.

explain.text: £12.996 lies between £12.99 and £13.00, only 0.004 below £13.00. Rounding 99 pennies up gives 100 pennies, a whole pound. So it shows as £13.00.

items.title: A short position when the price rises
items.prose: You are short 150 shares, a position of −150. The price rises from £8.40 to £8.65.
items.question: What is your P&L, in pounds?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Multiply the position by the price change.

byKey.sign: You treated the rise as good for you. You are short, so a rise is a loss.
byKey.price-not-change: You multiplied by the new price. P&L uses the change, +£0.25.

explain.text: The change is $8.65 - 8.40 = 0.25$. Then $(-150) \times 0.25 = -37.50$. A short position loses when the price rises.

items.title: Drawdown across zero
items.prose: A strategy's running P&L peaks at +£45.50. Later it sinks to a low of −£18.25.
items.question: By how many pounds did it fall from the peak to the low?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Work out the peak minus the low.

byKey.no-sign: You took 18.25 from 45.50 and ignored the sign of the low. The fall crosses zero, so the sizes add.
byKey.negative: You have the size right. Quote a drawdown as the size of the fall: 63.75.

explain.text: Peak minus low is $45.50 - (-18.25) = 45.50 + 18.25 = 63.75$. It fell £45.50 to zero and £18.25 below it.

items.title: Fractions and decimals in order
items.question: Which list is in order, smallest first?

options.why: You took $\tfrac13$ as 0.3 or less. It is $0.333\ldots$, just above 0.3.
You put $\tfrac13$ above 0.34. But $0.333\ldots$ has 3 hundredths, and 0.34 has 4.
You treated $\tfrac38$ as small because of the 8. It is 0.375, the largest.
